issues.title: The NVRAM write is a non-atomic whole-file rewrite with no size authority: a short read or empty buffer replaces a calibration image with a prefix of itself
issues.fixSummary: Get the authoritative size inside the same su invocation and gate on it: sz=$(stat -c %s -- "$path" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$path"); refuse to patch unless sz >= 16 AND the read length equals sz. Replace run("cat '<tmp>' > '<path>'") with an argv-passed, size-bounded in-place write: new ProcessBuilder("su","-c","dd if=\"$0\" of=\"$1\" bs=4096 conv=notrunc,fsync", tmp.getAbsolutePath(), path). Then require stat -c %s unchanged, then cmp -s tmp path, then re-derive the MAC from the offset patch() matched. Add if (data.length == 0) return false; at the top of writeRoot. Do NOT call writeRoot unless java_core's verified-backup helper (C2) returned true. Emit one log line per path actually written carrying path + matched offset(s) + old->new (this is the data K11/M3 renders). NEVER mv into place: rename changes the SELinux label/owner/mode of a calibration file and needs create/rename permission plus the right type transition in /mnt/vendor/nvdata, /persist, /efs, /data/vendor.
issues.acceptance: grep -n "cat .*>" MainActivity.java shows no shell redirection targeting path; the write command contains conv=notrunc and an argv-passed path (not string-concatenated); stat or wc -c comparisons exist before AND after the write. With a stub su whose cat returns 40 of 512 bytes, the run logs a read-size/on-disk mismatch, writes nothing, and the target's content and mtime are unchanged.
issues.risk: A timeout/watchdog must NOT be added to the write command until this lands (see H4) or the timeout itself truncates the file. Using mv instead of in-place is forbidden. Applying dd without the size pre-check still lets a 0-byte tmp truncate nothing only by luck.

issues.title: The pre-write backup is not a precondition: its write result is discarded, it is not atomic or verified, and an empty or short backup is later installed over the calibration file
issues.fixSummary: Write the backup to name.tmp in the app-private dir, call getFD().sync(), close, re-read with readFile() and require Arrays.equals with the pre-image AND equal length, then renameTo the final name (rename inside getFilesDir() is safe; K4's SELinux caveat applies only to the NVRAM path). Return that boolean and consume it. When a backup already exists, re-validate its length against the target's on-disk size obtained in the same su call and re-create it on mismatch. In restore(), require data != null && data.length >= 16 && data.length == on-disk size and that the buffer contains a MAC-shaped field; skip and log otherwise. Never treat a bare .path sibling as proof that its backup is valid.
issues.acceptance: With getFilesDir()/nvram_backup made unwritable, a stub run of setMac logs 'backup failed, NVRAM untouched' and the target sha256 is unchanged. With a 0-byte file, and separately a 10-byte file plus .path sibling, placed in nvram_backup, tapping Restore leaves the 512-byte target byte-identical in both cases. A stub kill during writeFile leaves no file that restore() will accept.
issues.risk: writeFile's atomicity fix must not be duplicated inside java_write, or the two stages will diverge; java_write only consumes the boolean. renameTo inside getFilesDir() is safe but must not be used on the NVRAM path.

issues.title: patch() has no degenerate-pattern guard and no replacement cap: an all-zero or all-0xFF runtime MAC rewrites about 90% of the calibration image
issues.fixSummary: Guard the PATTERN, not the user's input: ob is always macToBytes(getRuntimeMac()) (:732) / macToBytes(curRt) (:791), so the typed MAC is never the search pattern. In patch(), before any replacement, reject a degenerate oldB: require (oldB[0] & 1) == 0, at least one non-zero octet, and not all-0xFF; return a sentinel (e.g. -1) that the callers log as 'refusing to patch: MAC pattern is degenerate'. Replace the hits > 0 gate with hits > 0 && hits <= CAP, CAP validated against a real device dump (start at 8); above CAP abandon that file entirely - no backup, no write - and log 'unexpected layout - N matches, refusing', recording the distinct match offsets. After building the patched buffer assert data.length == orig.length and that every byte outside the recorded replacement windows is identical to orig. Separately reject all-zero, all-0xFF and multicast values as a TARGET in isMac() call sites, but do not reject locally-administered targets: randomMac() sets bit 0x02 at :777.
issues.acceptance: A harness calling patch() with an all-zero and an all-0xFF pattern on a 512-byte padded image returns the refusal sentinel, logs the refusal, and leaves the buffer byte-identical. Verified baseline on the current code: hits=78 / 468 of 512 bytes changed (all-zero) and hits=83 / 498 of 512 bytes changed (all-0xFF). grep shows the unicast / non-zero / not-all-0xFF check before the first replaceAll call and a hits > CAP abandon branch.
issues.risk: Setting CAP too low silently refuses to patch real devices: a legitimate file can hold a raw copy, a reversed copy and two ASCII copies. Rejecting locally-administered TARGETS breaks the Random button.

issues.title: CLI restore fabricates a 'factory' backup out of the live spoofed NVRAM, reports a successful restore, and can truncate the calibration file
issues.fixSummary: Make capture explicit: init_backup create|require. set/random call create; restore calls require and dies with 'no factory backup at $BAK - capture it before spoofing, or restore the factory MAC you recorded elsewhere'; show creates nothing and prints '(no backup)'. Never label a capture 'factory' when get_runtime differs from the captured MAC - that is direct evidence of a live spoof: print the mismatch and require an explicit 'backup --assume-factory' acknowledgement, or accept a factory MAC typed by the user. Restore must be in-place and length-checked, never cp: [ "$(wc -c <"$BAK")" -eq "$(wc -c <"$NV")" ] || die 'backup size mismatch', then $BB dd if="$BAK" of="$NV" bs=4096 conv=notrunc,fsync, then cmp -s "$BAK" "$NV" || die, then print the MAC re-read from $NV (never get_factory). Store $BAK.sha256 at capture and verify before writing back. Exit non-zero when the requested MAC is not in place afterwards. Add umask 077, mkdir -m 700 -p "$DIR" and chmod 600 "$BAK".
issues.acceptance: Reproduced baseline: with a 40-byte NVRAM holding the spoof 02:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee and no backup, 'restore' printed '[*] saved factory NVRAM backup' then '[*] restored factory NVRAM MAC: 02:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee' and exited 0 while the NVRAM was byte-identical; 'show' created a 0644 WIFI.factory holding the spoof. After the fix both must print an error and leave od -An -tx1 of the NVRAM unchanged. A 10-byte backup over a 40-byte NVRAM must die with a size mismatch and leave the file at 40 bytes (baseline: truncated to 10 bytes, exit 0). 'sh cli/macchanger.sh show' must create nothing under $DIR (diff find before/after).
issues.risk: Removing the implicit backup changes behaviour users may rely on, so the new explicit 'backup' subcommand must be documented. Refusing to write when no backup exists must not leave the user unable to restore a KNOWN factory MAC - hence the typed-MAC path in H1 and the --assume-factory acknowledgement.

issues.title: The signing private key ships with the distribution and verifiably signed the shipped APK; build.sh silently generates a different key when it is absent
issues.fixSummary: Remove app/ks.jks from anything distributed and delete the password line from README.md:35. Make signing explicit: KS=${KS:?supply a release keystore}, KS_PASS=${KS_PASS:?}; if the keystore is absent, die with an explicit INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE / 'uninstall first, after copying your backup out of /data/data/com.macchanger/files/nvram_backup/' warning and require a --new-key argument to generate one. Add -storetype PKCS12 (and rename to ks.p12) so the format does not depend on the deployed JDK. Print keytool -printcert -jarfile "$OUT" and sha256sum "$OUT" at the end of every build. Publish the release certificate SHA-256 in the README and state the Janus (CVE-2017-13156) caveat for API 21-23, where v2/v3 are ignored.
issues.acceptance: git ls-files and find . -name 'ks.jks' show no keystore in the shipped tree; grep -rn 'pass:android|pass: android' returns nothing in code or docs; running bash app/build.sh with no KS prints the refusal and exits non-zero WITHOUT creating a keystore; a build with a supplied keystore prints both the APK SHA-256 and the signer certificate SHA-256. Recorded baselines: APK signer SHA-256 8F:ED:CA:F1:8E:92:BB:19:24:E5:DE:1C:BB:A5:EA:6F:8B:31:FB:03:91:08:EE:AF:FC:4F:9C:F5:11:86:F1:AF, serial f95c6faeadff3f8d, identical to keytool -list -v -keystore app/ks.jks -storepass android.
issues.risk: Do not withdraw the key before the recovery path is durable (C2/H1): a user with the shipped APK installed who then builds with a different key hits INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE, and the only fix is uninstall, which deletes the app's backup. C5's loud refusal must be unmistakable and H1/C2 should land first or together.

issues.title: K1: factory record and NVRAM backups live in app-private storage, are destroyed by uninstall, and there is no way to enter a known factory MAC
issues.fixSummary: Make /data/adb/macchanger/ the primary record location for both front ends. Java has no file-API access there, so go through the root channel the app already uses: su -c 'mkdir -m 700 -p /data/adb/macchanger', then write/read WIFI.factory, WIFI.factory.path and a new factory.txt via argv-passed paths, batching round trips to keep the su count down. Keep the app-private dir as a fallback mirror for devices without /data/adb. Add a factory-MAC input row: when no record exists, accept a typed MAC, validate with isMac(), label it 'unverified - typed by user', and allow restore from it. Add an Export action that copies the record to a user-visible path through the existing root channel (su -c 'cp -a /data/adb/macchanger/WIFI.factory /sdcard/Download/') - no manifest permission, no res/, no new dependency.
issues.acceptance: With the app's private data removed (delete getFilesDir() in a stub run), restore() still finds the factory record under /data/adb/macchanger/ and reports its provenance; the factory row accepts a typed MAC and a restore from it succeeds; grep -n getFilesDir MainActivity.java shows the app dir used only as a fallback; AndroidManifest.xml still has zero <uses-permission> elements.
issues.risk: Relocating to /data/adb multiplies su invocations, each an independent prompt/timeout chance: batch them. Create the directory privately (mkdir -m 700) - never let mkdir -p leave /data/adb world-traversable. Keep the app-private mirror as a fallback for roots without /data/adb.

issues.title: K2: the factory value is captured from the live runtime MAC, so a randomized or already-spoofed MAC is recorded as 'factory'
issues.fixSummary: Derive the factory bytes from the NVRAM pre-image, not from /sys: patch() already sees orig, so require the 6 bytes at the matched offset to equal cur before writing, and record bytesToMac of orig AT THE MATCHED OFFSET. Refuse capture when (b[0] & 0x02) != 0 (locally administered), when the value is all-zero or all-0xFF, or when the runtime MAC is absent from every candidate NVRAM path - log 'runtime MAC looks randomized/spoofed; factory value not recorded - enter it manually' and surface H1's manual-entry row. Persist provenance in a factory_src pref (path + '@' + offset, or 'typed') and render the row as 'factory (NVRAM @0x4)' / 'factory (typed, unverified)' / '(not recorded)'. Never overwrite an existing record.
issues.acceptance: With a stub /sys value of 02:11:22:33:44:55 (locally administered) and no pref, setMac logs the refusal and leaves the factory pref unset. With a stub NVRAM whose factory MAC deliberately differs from the /sys string, the recorded factory value equals the NVRAM bytes and not the /sys string - asserted in the stub run. The provenance string appears in the UI row.
issues.risk: The locally-administered rejection applies ONLY to the captured factory value, never to the target MAC: randomMac() sets bit 0x02, so a shared rule would break the Random button.

issues.title: K12: restore's verdict comes from the runtime MAC, so 'Restored' is printed while the NVRAM still holds the spoof
issues.fixSummary: Base the verdict on the write, which the code can already verify. Count only content-verified writes; after each successful install re-read the file and re-derive the MAC at the matched offset to prove the factory bytes are present. Make the two strategies additive instead of mutually exclusive: run step 1 per path, and for any path where step 1 matched nothing but a valid backup exists, use the backup - do not gate step 2 on a global 'restored == 0'. Print two separate facts: 'NVRAM restored (verified: factory MAC present at 0x...)' and, when the runtime still differs, 'runtime not re-read yet - reboot or toggle WiFi to apply'. Early-return when the runtime MAC already equals the factory pref AND no NVRAM occurrence exists, to avoid a pointless destructive rewrite.
issues.acceptance: A stub run where the NVRAM write succeeds but the driver keeps reporting the spoof prints the NVRAM-verified success line and the 'runtime not re-read yet' note - never the bare 'Restored:' toast. A stub run with a valid backup for a path whose live MAC is not in the file still restores that path (proves step 2 is reachable after a partial step 1). patch(x,x) producing zero byte changes does not increment the restored count (verified current behaviour: hits=1, bytesChanged=false).
issues.risk: None beyond the general write-path risk; the fix removes a false success rather than adding a new write.

issues.title: K6: no shell timeout and no cancellation anywhere - and the obvious 'add a timeout to run()' is unsafe on the write path
issues.fixSummary: Add Res runTimed(String cmd, long ms) returning exit code + output, draining stdout on the calling thread with a deadline and a watchdog thread that calls destroyForcibly(); route run(), readRoot() and getprop() through it (default 15000 ms, a longer explicit budget for whole-image reads) and return the exit code so callers can distinguish failure from empty (see M4). Gate refresh() (:668) and the badge (:216) with if (busy) { toast("busy..."); return; } and disable the header buttons while busy, so one action is one serialized su stream. Log a red 'su did not answer - nothing was written' on timeout instead of returning a silent empty value. CRITICAL SEQUENCING: java_core runs BEFORE java_write, so C1's in-place dd write does not exist yet - apply the deadline to run()/readRoot()/getprop() but EXPLICITLY EXEMPT writeRoot's command, with a code comment stating why. java_ui (which runs last, after C1 has landed) extends the deadline to the write path.
issues.acceptance: With a stub su that never exits and never writes, tapping Set MAC returns the UI to a usable state within the timeout, logs the timeout line, clears busy, and a second tap is accepted. grep -n destroyForcibly finds a watchdog; grep -n 'waitFor(' shows a deadline. Inspection confirms writeRoot's own su invocation was left un-deadlined by java_core (comment present) and that java_ui only wired it after the conv=notrunc write landed.
issues.risk: THE MOST DANGEROUS ORDERING MISTAKE IN THIS PLAN: a uniform timeout applied before C1 truncates the calibration file, because su is killed after the shell has opened the destination with O_TRUNC but before it finishes. writeRoot's command must stay un-deadlined in java_core.

issues.title: A1+K9: 'cmd wifi status | head -3' cannot see the SSID on Android 12+, and an unresolved SSID is then read as 'this network randomizes the MAC'
issues.fixSummary: Stop slicing lines: run 'cmd wifi status' whole, extract with an anchored match on the 'Wifi is connected to ' prefix, strip the surrounding double quotes that WifiInfo.getSSID() adds, match 'Wifi is not connected' explicitly, treat '<unknown ssid>' as unknown, and return a distinct 'not connected' state instead of "". In privacyValue(), add ssid.isEmpty() to the guard (keep the em-dash case), skip element 0 (for (int b = 1; b < blocks.length; b++)), and match the SSID against the exact <string name="SSID">...</string> element inside one <Network> block after XML-unescaping both sides (& < > " ') with plain String.replace - no dependency. Return a tri-state "0"/"1"/"2"/"3"/"?" and let a positive value only EXPLAIN a failure, never override it; when the SSID is unknown print 'driver kept it (randomization state unknown)'.
issues.acceptance: A harness calling privacyValue(storeWhereAllNetworksAre0, "") returns "?" - baseline on current code returns "1" deterministically (xml.split("<Network>")[0] is the preamble, blk.contains("") is always true, and the preamble has no MacRandomizationSetting so :640 fires). With a store whose SSID is 'Ben & Jerry' and a cmd wifi status reporting 'Wifi is connected to "Ben & Jerry"', the row resolves to that network's real setting rather than unknown/randomized. grep -n 'head -3|1,3p' MainActivity.java returns nothing. AOSP verification: as root the printStatus order is 'Wifi is enabled' / 'Wifi scanning is ...' / '==== ClientModeManager instance: ... ====' / 'Wifi is connected to "<SSID>"' (android12:1454, android14:2404, android16:2888 privilege branch; SSID at :2866 inside printWifiInfo), so head -3 yields zero matches; android11-release has no privilege branch, which is why the test device hid this.
issues.risk: XML unescaping must be conservative: do not URL-decode, trim internal whitespace or case-fold, or an over-eager normalisation can match a DIFFERENT network and re-introduce the wrong-block bug being fixed.

issues.title: K5: the CLI hardcodes offset 4 and verifies by re-reading that offset, so verification is circular
issues.fixSummary: Precondition the write: cur4=$(mac_from "$NV"), require [ "$cur4" = "$(get_runtime)" ], and otherwise refuse with the bytes actually found printed - or adopt the APK's approach and scan the whole file for the runtime MAC bytes, staying dependency-free with $BB hexdump/od. Generate the bytes portably as POSIX octal - verified correct under BOTH dash and busybox: printf "%b" "\0004\0371\0223\0021\0066\0277" yields 04 f9 93 11 36 bf - built with $BB awk (already required at :86). Add count=6 to the dd. Verify NON-CIRCULARLY: hexdump a whole 16-byte window around the offset before and after and compare against the expected whole-window image, so the check covers what changed rather than only what was written. Have cmd_set exit non-zero when the post-restart runtime MAC differs from the requested one.
issues.acceptance: On-device, 'busybox printf "%b" "\x41" | od -An -tx1' returns 41 (safe) rather than 5c 78 34 31 (broken). A sandbox run where the runtime MAC is absent from offset 4 makes set refuse and leaves the file byte-identical (verified baseline for the hazard: dd bs=1 seek=4 conv=notrunc extended a 4-byte file to 14 bytes). grep -n 'seek=4' cli/macchanger.sh shows count=6 on the same command. cmd_set exits non-zero when the runtime MAC is unchanged after reinit_wifi (test with a stubbed svc).
issues.risk: The \xHH escape failure is NOT demonstrated for the shipped path: the code calls busybox's printf applet, not the shell builtin, and busybox 1.30.1 expands it correctly (the dash-builtin test cited by an auditor does not exercise the code under audit). It is rated a hardening item, not a demonstrated break. Do not substitute a hardcoded offset for the scan.

issues.title: K10: the WiFi restart is blind sleeps around a toggle whose result is discarded, so a legal no-op is reported as the driver refusing the MAC
issues.fixSummary: Replace both sleeps with polling for the actual state: issue the toggle via 'cmd wifi set-wifi-enabled disabled' (falling back to 'svc wifi disable'), then poll the first line of 'cmd wifi status' for 'Wifi is disabled'/'Wifi is enabled' every 500 ms up to about 10 s, and only then read the runtime MAC. If the state never changes, abort the verdict with a specific message ('WiFi did not toggle - airplane mode on?') and do NOT run the ip-link fallback. Apply the same sequencing to reinit_wifi (cli:53-57), which can poll /sys/class/net/$IF/operstate or cmd wifi status. Keep it in-process: no new permission, no foreground service, no res/.
issues.acceptance: With a stub cmd wifi status reporting 'Wifi is disabled' for the first 3 polls then 'Wifi is enabled', the app proceeds after about 1.5 s instead of 9.5 s and logs the observed transitions. With a stub that always reports 'Wifi is enabled', it logs 'WiFi did not toggle' and issues NO ip link set command (assert with a logging stub su). grep -n 'sleep(' MainActivity.java shows no fixed sleep on the WiFi-restart path. Platform evidence: WifiSettingsStore.handleWifiToggled contains 'if (mAirplaneModeOn && !isAirplaneToggleable()) return false;' (android16 WifiSettingsStore.java:257-260), so svc wifi can be a legal no-op; note cmd wifi set-wifi-enabled also discards the boolean and returns 0, so state must be verified either way.
issues.risk: None: removing blind sleeps shortens the destructive window and reduces the rotation race (M2). Polling must have a hard cap so a dead HAL cannot hang the worker - rely on H4's deadline.

issues.title: K8: the crash-prone ip link fallback is used to fabricate a success verdict and is never labelled non-persistent
issues.fixSummary: Gate the fallback behind an explicit opt-in in the SET MAC card (off by default, with the MTK warning shown verbatim) and run it only when the NVRAM write produced no verified change. When it runs, the log and toast must say 'runtime only - NOT persistent, will not survive reboot'; keep the green verdict and the 'MAC set:' toast exclusively for a content-verified NVRAM write. Never run it when the WiFi toggle did not take (H7) or when a candidate file existed but was unreadable (M4). If the platform reports the interface does not exist, report unsupported device (M5) rather than attempting it.
issues.acceptance: With any == false and an intercepting stub su, the log contains 'runtime only' and 'NOT persistent', the toast is not 'MAC set:', and no ip link set command is issued unless the opt-in was enabled. grep -n 'ip link set' MainActivity.java shows the command constructed behind the toggle guard. Recorded baseline: cli/macchanger.sh:74-75 documents the identical command as crashing the MTK WiFi service, while MainActivity.java:848-850 uses it as its apply fallback and :757-758 then toasts success.
issues.risk: On MTK the fallback can crash the WiFi service - the state the app is least able to recover from, since its own recovery depends on WiFi coming back. Gating it is the mitigation; do not delete it outright, because on Qualcomm/Samsung/Unisoc it is the only path that applies a MAC when the NVRAM layout is unknown.

issues.title: build.sh discards javac's exit status, so step [1/6] can never fail
issues.fixSummary: Use set -euo pipefail and capture javac's status without disturbing it: out=$(javac ... 2>&1); st=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v 'source value 8|target value 8|deprecat' || true; [ $st -eq 0 ] || { echo 'javac failed (see above)'; exit 1; }. Simpler and better: drop the pipe and pass -Xlint:-options (the README already requires openjdk-21) so plain set -e does its job. Add [ -f "$AJ" ] || { echo "android.jar not found: $AJ (is \$PREFIX set?)"; exit 1; } near :5 and the same check for FRAMEWORK=/system/framework/framework-res.apk. Assert the compile produced the expected class: [ -s build/classes.txt ] || exit 1 and [ -f build/classes/com/macchanger/MainActivity.class ] || exit 1.
issues.acceptance: With a deliberate syntax error in MainActivity.java, ./build.sh prints the javac error, exits non-zero, and does NOT print 'BUILT:'. With 'env -u PREFIX ./build.sh' it prints the android.jar message and exits non-zero. bash -n app/build.sh passes. Resolved contradiction: 'javac emits no class files at all when any compilation unit errors' is WRONG - reproduced here with JDK 17.0.20, 'javac -d out Good.java Bad.java' emitted out/Good.class while 'javac -d out Bad.java Good.java' emitted nothing, so the behaviour is order dependent and a partial class set is reachable once a second source file exists.
issues.risk: set -o pipefail is bash-specific. The shebang is the Termux bash, so it is fine for ./build.sh; document that the script must be run that way rather than 'sh build.sh', or a dash invocation breaks the new guard.

issues.title: A5: the randomization value space is 0-3, AUTO=3 is the field default, and the app handles only 0/1/2
issues.fixSummary: Map "3" explicitly to 'auto (framework decides)' and treat 1/2/3 as 'may randomize' in isRandomized(). Read the config store once and enumerate every <Network> block (plain root cat, no permission, no resources) so the privacy row can say 'randomized on N of M saved networks', keeping the existing tap-through to WiFi settings. Combine with H5's tri-state return and XML unescaping rather than adding a second parser.
issues.acceptance: A harness on a store containing a network with value="3" returns "3" and isRandomized() is true for it. With a store of 3 networks of which 2 are randomized, the privacy row's text names that count. AOSP verification: RANDOMIZATION_NONE=0 / PERSISTENT=1 / NON_PERSISTENT=2 / AUTO=3 with 'public int macRandomizationSetting = RANDOMIZATION_AUTO;' (android12:1652-1684, android14:1802-1829, android16:1879-1906).
issues.risk: None. Read-only change; the multi-network enumeration must not write anything or add a permission.

issues.title: busy is an Activity instance field and rotation is enabled, so a config change mid-operation starts a second concurrent operation
issues.fixSummary: Make the lock process-wide (static volatile boolean busy), reflect it in onCreate by disabling/annotating the action buttons while an operation is in flight, and add android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|keyboardHidden" so rotation does not recreate the Activity mid-operation (this also keeps the log visible). Add a dependency-free cross-process lock in the directory both front ends can use - /data/adb/macchanger/lock: mkdir succeeds or fails atomically, so acquire with su -c 'mkdir /data/adb/macchanger/lock' plus a PID+timestamp staleness check, release in a finally, and use the same lock in cmd_set/cmd_restore/init_backup with a trap for cleanup.
issues.acceptance: Rotating the device during a Set MAC - or an instrumented stub run that completes onCreate a second time while the first worker is alive - does not start a second worker: assert exactly one su stream and one reinitWifi per operation using a logging stub. A second CLI invocation while the app holds the lock exits non-zero with 'another macchanger operation is running' and writes nothing. The window is 9.5-16.5 s today (H7), which is what makes the race ordinary rather than exotic.
issues.risk: Do not solve this with a foreground service: that requires FOREGROUND_SERVICE (plus a type on API 34+) and destroys the zero-permission property. The mkdir lock must carry a staleness check or a killed process leaves the device permanently locked out of both front ends.

issues.title: K11: the log keeps 8 lines, shows 6 when expanded, and never names the patched NVRAM path
issues.fixSummary: Raise the ring buffer to at least 50 entries and render ALL retained lines when expanded (setMaxLines(logLines.size()) or a fixed larger cap) so nothing retained is invisible. Add a long-press 'copy log' using ClipboardManager (no permission) so the user can preserve it. The per-path detail - path + matched offset(s) + old->new - is emitted by java_write as part of C1; this stage renders it. Keep newest-first order and the existing colour scheme.
issues.acceptance: A Set MAC touching two paths produces two log lines, each containing the path string and an offset (baseline today: 'nvram patched (N hit)' with no path, MainActivity.java:750). grep -n 'size() > 8' MainActivity.java shows the raised cap. Expanding the bar after 10 operations shows more than 6 lines (baseline: cap 8 at :345 but only 6 rendered at :304).
issues.risk: None. Purely additive UI change, no new dependency and no res/.

issues.title: A read/write denial or a failed root probe is reported as 'no nvram match - runtime only', i.e. as if the device were unsupported
issues.fixSummary: Probe each candidate in ONE su round trip and print per-path state: for p in ...; do if [ -e "$p" ]; then r=ok; w=ok; [ -r "$p" ] || r=denied; [ -w "$p" ] || w=denied; echo "$p r=$r w=$w"; else echo "$p absent"; fi; done - plus the mount options of the containing filesystem from /proc/mounts so a read-only mount is visible. Distinguish four outcomes in the final message: no candidate on this device (name the paths probed); candidate found but not readable/writable (name the errno or mount option); patched (name the path); patched but readback unreadable -> red 'patched but verification unreadable - re-check before rebooting'. Abort before any WiFi restart when the enumeration itself failed, and never run the ip-link fallback then. Cheap partial step needing no refactor: if !any and !run("id").contains("uid=0"), print 'no root - nothing was attempted'.
issues.acceptance: With a stub su that denies reads, the log names the paths probed and the denial instead of 'no nvram match', and no WiFi restart is issued. With a stub where the write succeeds but the verification read returns empty, the log says 'patched but verification unreadable' rather than 'no nvram match' - baseline today folds that case into 'no nvram match - runtime only' (MainActivity.java:751, :816) even though the file was modified. A genuinely unsupported device prints the distinct no-candidate message with the probed list.
issues.risk: Keep it to one su round trip per probe batch: extra invocations multiply the timeout/prompt exposure H4 describes.

issues.title: The detected vendor never affects behaviour, there is no unsupported-device verdict, and targetSdk 30 must deliberately stay
issues.fixSummary: Use socName() for behaviour, not decoration: order and filter the candidate list per detected vendor and record the vendor in the log. Add an explicit terminal state - when existingNvram() is empty, or no path contains the runtime MAC, show 'UNSUPPORTED DEVICE - nothing was written. Looked for: <paths with missing/unreadable/MAC-not-found>' built from M4's per-path report, and require H8's explicit opt-in before any ip-link fallback. Record in a manifest comment and in the README WHY targetSdk 30 is deliberate (installs on Android 14-16; raising it requires adding inset padding). Java-only, existing helpers, no permission, no res/.
issues.acceptance: On a stub device with none of the nine paths present, the UI shows the UNSUPPORTED DEVICE state listing the probed paths and issues no WiFi restart and no ip link command. With a MediaTek soc string, MTK paths are probed before Qualcomm/Samsung/Unisoc and the log names the vendor. grep -n targetSdkVersion app/AndroidManifest.xml still reads 30, with an explanation present. Negative result (verified in AOSP): MIN_INSTALLABLE_TARGET_SDK is M(23) on android14 (PackageManagerService.java:570) and 'Flags.minTargetSdk24() ? N : M' (24) on android15:565-566 / android16:570-571, and the deprecation-dialog threshold MIN_SUPPORTED_TARGET_SDK_INT resolves to 28, so targetSdk 30 installs and launches with no dialog on Android 14-16.
issues.risk: Do NOT raise targetSdk: at 35 Android 15 enforces edge-to-edge and this hand-built layout uses fixed paddings (MainActivity.java:192, :297-299) with no inset handling anywhere (no WindowInsets, no setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener, no configChanges), so the title row and log bar would sit under the system bars; Android 16 drops the opt-out.

issues.title: The CLI rewrites NVRAM even when the runtime MAC is unknown, and wlan0 is hardcoded in both front ends
issues.fixSummary: Resolve the interface instead of assuming it: derive from 'cmd wifi status' / 'iw dev' / 'ls /sys/class/net | grep ^wlan', and die with 'cannot determine the WiFi interface; use --iface=NAME' when zero or more than one candidate exists unless explicitly forced. Add an --iface option. In the app, detect the same way, show the interface in the DEVICE card, and use it for the address read, the refresh and the fallback so the failure is self-describing rather than 'cannot parse MAC'.
issues.acceptance: With a stub environment where no wlan* interface exists, 'macchanger.sh set ...' refuses with the interface message and leaves the NVRAM's content and mtime unchanged (baseline: it writes offset 4 blind and then prints an empty runtime MAC while reporting success). With two wlan* interfaces it refuses unless --iface is given. The app displays the detected interface name.
issues.risk: Multi-interface reporting is fine; blind multi-interface WRITING is not. Detect and report, and require an explicit interface choice before writing anything - writing the wrong NVRAM is worse than not supporting AP mode.

issues.title: Shell failure text is returned as data and shown as the MAC; root detection cannot tell 'denied' from 'not installed'; paths are pasted into a root shell
issues.fixSummary: Return status, not text: a small 'static final class Res { final int code; final String out; boolean ok(); }' from run()/readRoot() (Process.exitValue() is already available after waitFor). At every display site, if (!isMac(rt)) { log("cannot read " + IFACE + " (WiFi off, or root denied)", C_BAD); return; } instead of rendering the error as a MAC. Make checkRoot distinguish three outcomes by probing /system/bin/su, /debug_ramdisk/su, /sbin/su then PATH and passing the resolved absolute path to ProcessBuilder: found+exit0 = granted; found+exit!=0 = 'root denied'; not found = 'su is not installed - this app cannot work on this device'. Delete the duplicate read so getRuntimeMac and refresh cannot diverge. Harden: never interpolate a path into shell text - new ProcessBuilder("su","-c","cat -- \"$0\"", path) for reads and "cat -- \"$0\" > \"$1\"", tmp, path for writes - plus a whitelist gate 'if (!nvramPaths().contains(path)) return false;' re-checked after reading a .path file in restore.
issues.acceptance: A stub su that denies makes the runtime row show a clear 'cannot read wlan0 (WiFi off, or root denied)' and never the stderr text, and no toast reads 'driver gave <error text>' (baseline: getRuntimeMac() returns 'cat: /sys/class/net/wlan0/address: No such file or directory', rendered at :691, :764, :765). With no su binary at all the UI says 'su is not installed' rather than 'not granted'. A stub /system/bin/su that exists but exits 1 yields 'root denied'. grep -n "cat '" MainActivity.java returns no path interpolated into shell text, and grep -n 'nvramPaths().contains' shows the write whitelist. Negative results kept: isMac() rejects every realistic failure string, so no error text can reach macToBytes() or the factory pref; and injection is not exploitable in the shipped build because every path traces to the hardcoded nvramPaths() constants.
issues.risk: Latent injection becomes live the moment a candidate path is made configurable or derived from a getprop - it would run as the same root shell that rewrites calibration partitions. Do not add an Intent/extras API: MainActivity never reads an Intent today, and one would let any app on the device inject into run().

issues.title: No build identity and no post-sign verification
issues.fixSummary: Stamp identity at build time via aapt (--version-code $(date +%Y%m%d) --version-name 1.0+$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo nogit)), print sha256sum "$OUT" and keytool -printcert -jarfile "$OUT" at the end, and display the app's own versionName plus lastUpdateTime from getPackageManager().getPackageInfo(getPackageName(), 0) in the DEVICE card (API 21-safe, no permission, no resources). Add a launch icon WITHOUT a res/ directory by referencing a framework drawable: android:icon="@android:drawable/ic_menu_manage". Add post-sign gates - aapt list "$OUT" | grep -q classes.dex || exit 1; zipalign -c -v 4 "$OUT" || exit 1; aapt dump badging "$OUT" | grep -q launchable-activity || exit 1 - and wrap the post-sign region in trap 'rm -f "$OUT"' ERR (or sign to a temp name and mv after verification).
issues.acceptance: ./build.sh prints the APK SHA-256 and the signer certificate SHA-256 (recorded baseline: APK SHA-256 1760a8cb0d78ba68c83eed14214f3ee0c77d5144cdcf2c494025d7407937a6da). The DEVICE card shows a version string that changes between builds (baseline: versionCode 1 / versionName 1.0 frozen in the manifest and in the shipped binary, with no self-reported version in the app). aapt dump badging reports an application icon (baseline: no android:icon anywhere). Removing classes.dex from the aligned APK by hand makes the script fail at the new gate instead of printing 'BUILT:'. The zero-permission property must still hold: no <uses-permission> element in the built manifest.
issues.risk: New post-sign gates must not add a tool dependency: prefer 'aapt list' and 'zipalign -c' (both already required) over a bare unzip, and print a clear message if a helper is missing, or the on-device build breaks for users who installed exactly the documented packages.

issues.title: No offline regression harness exists, so every fix in this plan would be unverifiable and unprotected against reintroduction
issues.file: tools/ (new: verify.sh, extract_logic.py, logic_test.java, cli_test.sh, readme_claims_test.sh)
issues.lines: new files; nothing under app/ or cli/
issues.fixSummary: Add a dependency-free harness that runs fully offline and touches no app or CLI logic. tools/extract_logic.py pulls the pure methods (isMac, macToBytes, bytesToMac, hexPlain, reverse, replaceAll, patch, privacyValue) VERBATIM out of MainActivity.java into a generated Java file so the harness tests the shipped source text rather than a stale copy. tools/logic_test.java compiles against minimal android.* stubs and asserts the invariants this plan depends on: degenerate all-zero / all-0xFF patterns are refused; patch preserves length and every byte outside match windows; patch(x,x) reports zero byte changes; privacyValue(store, "") is "?"; uppercase and plain-hex ASCII copies are handled; replaceAll never overruns. tools/cli_test.sh synthesises NVRAM files and runs a constants-redirected copy of cli/macchanger.sh with stub busybox/svc, asserting no implicit backup creation from show/restore, restore refusing a size-mismatched backup, set refusing when the target offset does not hold the runtime MAC, and the file surviving byte-identically on every refusal. tools/readme_claims_test.sh greps the claims this audit corrected (keystore password in docs, 'head -3', 'pass:android', targetSdkVersion, the CLI's MTK-only scope) so doc/code drift is caught. javac + sh + busybox/od only: no Gradle, no network, no Android SDK, no res/.
issues.acceptance: sh tools/verify.sh runs on this machine with only JDK 17 and busybox and exits 0 on the fixed tree. Run against a copy of /root/macchanger-fixed/.pristine it fails with a specific message for each of C3, H3, H5 and H6, proving the harness detects the defects it guards. The APK cannot be rebuilt here, so the harness must never depend on aapt/d8/apksigner/zipalign.
issues.risk: The harness copies and rewrites source text, so extraction must be verified to have found every method it needs, or the tests could pass vacuously against an empty extraction. Assert the extracted file contains each expected method signature before compiling.

issues.title: README claims the code does not support, and omits what a root tool needs
issues.fixSummary: State up front 'CLI = MediaTek only; APK = candidate paths for MTK/Qualcomm/Samsung/Unisoc, tested only on MTK'. Move the ip-link sentence out of 'What it does' and mark it a last-resort fallback that can kill the WiFi service on MTK and does not survive a reboot. Soften the randomization claim to 'attempts to detect, and cannot on Android 12+ without a connected network'. Delete the keystore password line, document the required android.jar API level and the two signing identities, and correct the false 'always copies the original NVRAM before writing' claim after C2. Add: supported devices and an explicit Android ceiling, per-vendor risk, what to do when the backup is lost, how to verify the APK by hash and signer fingerprint, what to do when WiFi stops working entirely, and M5's deliberate targetSdk 30 note.
issues.acceptance: grep -n 'pass: android|pass:android' README.md returns nothing. The README contains 'MediaTek only' next to the CLI section and 'does not survive a reboot' next to the ip-link mention. The randomization section states the Android 12+ limitation. The build section names an android.jar API level and both signing identities.
issues.risk: Sequencing: docs is the last stage. Do not publish a certificate fingerprint before build has stopped shipping ks.jks, and do not restate the keystore password in any new file.

issues.title: No LICENSE, SECURITY.md or CHANGELOG, and the version stamp is frozen
issues.fixSummary: Add LICENSE (MIT or GPL-3.0), SECURITY.md (contact plus scope: 'this app runs as root and rewrites Wi-Fi calibration; reports about the shipped signing key are security issues') and CHANGELOG.md keyed to versionCode, recording the APK SHA-256 and signer certificate SHA-256 per entry. Bump versionCode/versionName for every APK added to prebuilt/ - the manifest is the only version metadata an APK carries here - and state which source commit the shipped APK corresponds to.
issues.acceptance: git ls-files shows LICENSE, SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md (baseline: exactly seven files, none of them). The newest changelog entry names the APK SHA-256 and signer SHA-256 and matches sha256sum prebuilt/MacChanger.apk (currently 1760a8cb0d78ba68c83eed14214f3ee0c77d5144cdcf2c494025d7407937a6da). The README names the source commit for the shipped APK (the current APK verifiably matches the current source - its dex contains the distinctive literals nvram patched, MacRandomizationSetting, write.tmp, nvram_backup, ip link set dev - but nothing records that).
issues.risk: None. Prose files only; no build or permission change.

issues.title: No intended-use/authorization statement
issues.fixSummary: Add a short 'Intended use / authorization' section stating factually: intended for devices you own and networks you are authorized to use (privacy, repair of a corrupted or zeroed factory MAC, testing your own equipment); the change is persistent, invisible to Android's per-network randomization setting, survives a factory reset, and only this app/CLI can undo it (with the recovery steps from C4/H1); do not use it to evade per-device billing, MAC allow/deny lists, captive-portal limits, or a block imposed by an operator who does not own the device, and note that some jurisdictions treat that as a computer-misuse offence. Keep the existing CLI multicast warning as the in-code model.
issues.acceptance: The README contains an 'Intended use' (or equivalent) heading whose text states the ownership/authorization boundary, the persistence-beyond-factory-reset property, and the recovery steps. The section is prose only - no code, permission or dependency change. Factual basis: the tool contains no attack primitives against anything but its own NIC (no scanning, deauthentication, injection or cloning of observed third-party MACs), and cli:81 already acknowledges the MAC is a credential.
issues.risk: None.

issues.title: CLI diagnostics: random does not validate its own output, and a missing busybox blames the NVRAM
issues.fixSummary: Capture into r then 'valid_mac "$r" || die "cannot generate a random MAC (busybox od/awk failed)"'. After the BB resolution at :18, fail early with the real cause: '$BB true 2>/dev/null || die "busybox not found: install it or set BB="'. Pure shell, dependency-free, existing flow preserved.
issues.acceptance: With BB pointed at a nonexistent binary, every subcommand dies immediately with the busybox message and no NVRAM path is touched (baseline: the user sees two 'not found' lines and then 'error: NVRAM write verification failed', which blames the NVRAM). With a stubbed failing od, random prints the od/awk message rather than 'error: usage: <script> set AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF'.
issues.risk: None.

issues.title: Screen privacy: the factory MAC and connected SSID land in the recents snapshot
issues.fixSummary: Add getWindow().setFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE, WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE); in onCreate BEFORE setContentView. No permission, no dependency, no res/, API 1. Optionally expose it as a toggle, default on.
issues.acceptance: grep -n FLAG_SECURE MainActivity.java finds it in onCreate before setContentView. On a device, the recents preview shows a secure card and screenshots are refused. This finding cannot be fully proven without a device; code inspection plus documented platform behaviour is the ceiling. Context: the only file-write sinks are app-private (MainActivity.java:412-421, :600-612), there is no android.util.Log / System.out / printStackTrace anywhere, and the manifest requests no permissions - so nothing leaks off-device today.
issues.risk: None. Do not add any permission or window flag that requires one.

issues.title: The root state machine is decorative: lastRoot is write-only, no-arg checkRoot() is dead, the badge tap can never refresh
issues.fixSummary: Read lastRoot at the top of setMac() and restore(): if !lastRoot, call checkRoot(true) and refuse with 'root required' instead of running the blind restart. Change the badge handler (:216) to checkRoot(true) so a grant refreshes the cards. Delete the unused no-arg checkRoot() (:652) and either use lastRoot or remove it. Make reinitWifi treat a value that fails isMac() as unknown and skip the fallback (H7/M7).
issues.acceptance: With su denied, tapping Set MAC logs/toasts 'root required' and issues no WiFi restart and no NVRAM write (assert via a logging stub su). Tapping the root badge on a device that then grants root populates the cards without a manual Refresh. grep -c lastRoot MainActivity.java shows it both read and written (baseline: written at :661, never read), and grep -n 'void checkRoot()' MainActivity.java returns nothing (baseline: dead at :652). Nothing corrupts today - writeRoot's read-back at :449-450 correctly refuses to claim success - so this is correctness of messaging, not data safety.
issues.risk: None.

workPackages.goal: Make the factory-MAC record and the pre-write backup durable and truthful, and make the root/shell layer honest. Relocate backups and the factory value to /data/adb/macchanger (keeping the app-private dir as a fallback mirror) and add manual factory entry plus export; derive the factory value from the NVRAM pre-image and refuse to capture a randomized/spoofed runtime MAC; make restore's verdict come from the verified write instead of the runtime MAC and make its two strategies additive; make the backup atomic, verified and a precondition; give the shell layer a Res status with per-path reporting, real su-probe diagnostics and a bounded, cancelable timeout - but leave writeRoot's own su command UN-deadlined, because java_write replaces the write primitive only in the next stage and a timeout there would truncate the partition. Also harden path handling (argv-passed paths, whitelist gate).

Make the NVRAM write path non-destructive and self-verifying. Gate every write on an authoritative on-disk size from the same su call; replace the truncating 'cat tmp > path' with an argv-passed, size-bounded in-place dd conv=notrunc,fsync followed by stat, cmp and a re-derivation of the MAC from the matched offset; never mv into place. Refuse degenerate patch patterns (all-zero / all-0xFF) and cap the match count per file, asserting length and out-of-window byte equality. Log the path, offset(s) and old->new for every write. Gate the ip-link fallback behind an explicit opt-in and stop it from producing a green success verdict.

Make the UI, diagnostics and WiFi restart tell the truth. Parse 'cmd wifi status' by content instead of line position (head -3 can never see the SSID on Android 12+ when run as root), fix privacyValue's empty-SSID wildcard and add XML unescaping and the AUTO=3 value, and stop reporting an unresolved SSID as MAC randomization. Poll for the real WiFi state instead of blind sleeps and verify the toggle took. Replace the one-size-fits-all 'no nvram match' with per-path status and an explicit unsupported-device verdict, and use the detected vendor to order candidates. Make the operation lock process-wide and survive rotation, grow and render the log fully, add FLAG_SECURE, and wire the root state machine. Finally, once java_write's dd write has landed, extend java_core's shell deadline to the write path.

Stop the CLI from inventing a factory value and from writing blind. Make backup capture explicit (create/require/--assume-factory) so restore and show never fabricate a 'factory' record from live spoofed state; make restore in-place, length-checked and verified against the target rather than circularly against the offset just written; precondition set on the bytes actually present at the target offset (or scan like the APK); generate MAC bytes portably as POSIX octal with a bounded dd; verify against a whole window rather than the single written offset; resolve the interface instead of assuming wlan0; and fix the busybox/random diagnostics.

Fix the trust and identity of the build. Get the signing private key out of the distributed tree, stop build.sh from silently generating a different key that forces an uninstall (which destroys the user's only backup), require an externally supplied keystore with a loud refusal otherwise, and pin the store type. Make javac's exit status actually fail the build, validate android.jar and framework-res.apk up front, assert the expected class was produced, stamp versionCode/versionName per build, print the APK SHA-256 and signer certificate SHA-256, add post-sign content/alignment/badging gates with a trap, and add a launch icon via a framework drawable without introducing res/.

Make the documentation match the code and cover what a root tool must document: CLI is MediaTek-only, the ip-link fallback is non-persistent and crash-prone on MTK, randomization detection cannot work on Android 12+ without a connected network, the keystore password line is gone, the android.jar API level and the two signing identities are stated, the 'always copies the original NVRAM' claim is corrected, and targetSdk 30 is documented as deliberate. Add LICENSE, SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md with per-release APK and certificate hashes, and an intended-use/authorization section.

Build the offline verification harness that makes every fix in this plan checkable and keeps it from regressing: extract the pure methods verbatim from MainActivity.java, compile them against android.* stubs and assert the write-path and parsing invariants (degenerate patterns refused, length and out-of-window bytes preserved, privacyValue(store,"") == "?", ASCII-form coverage, no replaceAll overrun); run a constants-redirected copy of the CLI against synthetic NVRAM files to assert no implicit backup creation, size-mismatch refusal and byte-identical refusals; and grep the doc/code claims this audit corrected. javac + sh + busybox only - no Gradle, no network, no Android SDK.
